observations.fact: At 8.8 B adds a dark rim around blue’s preparation ring. At 9.3 B has a white crossed marker on red while both panels show red at 80 HP; the log records blue fireball damage at 9.25. At 9.7 red’s attack region is visible in both and no corresponding white damage marker is visible on blue; logs show red releasing melee at 9.633 with no subsequent damage there.
observations.interpretation: The victim marker gives a useful answer to “did that connect?” beyond existing particles. It helps distinguish red’s failed swipe from blue’s payoff. The preparation difference is subtle at this overview scale; I cannot claim it made anticipation easy in motion.

observations.fact: At 11.3 the fighters overlap closely and B adds a dark floor ring. The final sampled state holds red’s win at about 12.217; B retains a crossed hit marker at blue’s final position while blue is absent. Logs record red’s melee hits at 11.433 and 12.217.
observations.interpretation: A distinct payoff remains after the target disappears, which is helpful. Red closing on a fireball user creates understandable contrasting roles in both versions. The generic markers themselves do little to strengthen magical identity or make the outcome a richer surprise.

observations.fact: At 6.6 both have orange fireballs, pale blue circular magic and a bright yellow cast area. At 7.0 B adds a white crossed marker where green was eliminated, plus a dark launch ring near yellow’s spread. At 7.3 orange projectiles and pale blue remnants are still visible without a white marker on red. At 7.6 B shows a crossed marker on red while both show 91 HP. Logs locate green’s death at 6.983, yellow’s spread release at 6.883 and yellow’s two hits on red at 7.567/7.600. At 8.6 both still show separated orange projectiles and the red/yellow close exchange.
observations.interpretation: B clarifies the two local consequences without replacing recognizable ice/fire silhouettes. The spell continuing into a changed crowd is promising as a magical surprise, but these samples do not establish whether a viewer follows its ownership. Marker presence confirms damage, not the unique projectile responsible.

observations.fact: B adds dark preparation rims to multiple fighters at 0.1; at 0.7 it adds dark rings near green and yellow. At 1.3 red and green overlap with pale blue circles and a hit marker on red while yellow’s small orange volley is visible elsewhere. At 2.3 the large ice shard/circles and orange projectile train remain recognizable in both; B adds a marker near the red/green overlap. Logs show green’s spread damage around 0.983–1.017, yellow’s gatling release at 0.7 and red’s melee damage at 2.167.
observations.interpretation: The extra marks remain compact in these samples, but several outlines cluster around the same small bodies. This is the contrary case: the viewer may learn who was hit while still struggling to tell which magic caused it. More simultaneous symbols do not by themselves create a stronger character identity.

Inconclusive as experienced surprise. The logs support consequences from established abilities, but samples do not demonstrate recognition or emotional payoff.

overallVerdict: B is worth putting before the owner as a modest readability improvement. It helps answer whether a spell connected, but does not yet make the magic more distinctive or establish better buildup and payoff in motion.

displaySummary.title: Hits are clearer; magical identity is mostly unchanged
displaySummary.text: I slightly prefer the added cues: they mark who actually got hurt while fire and ice remain visible. Crowded overlaps still make the source hard to follow. Stills cannot tell me whether the buildup feels better.
